clue.text: Great mob chucked fruit

indicators.note: something chucked is thrown about, so the letters of 'Great mob' land in a new order

explanation.surface: A huge crowd hurling fruit, perhaps at a hapless performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'chucked' the verb the mob performs on the fruit; in fact it only stirs the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergamot is a small citrus fruit whose rind oil flavours Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: Repeat what is expected — rubbish

parts.note: par is the expected score or standard, as in golf

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing a predictable, repeated line as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits the clue so it reads as a complaint about cliché, but it is just definition then two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words mechanically without understanding, as the talking bird does.

clue.text: After a month agent has modern technology falling apart

indicators.note: 'after a month' puts the agent's letters behind those of the month in the chain

parts.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: An agent whose modern gadgets break down after only a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling apart' looks like it describes the technology; it is the definition, an adjective phrase matching DECREPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decrepit is worn out and dilapidated through age or neglect, crumbling to pieces.

clue.text: Row in lake, intercepting ship

indicators.note: to intercept is to get in the way, so the lake sits in the middle of the ship

parts.note: Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A rowing boat on a lake cutting across a ship's path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as the verb for oars; it is the noun, a line of things in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A series is a sequence of similar things one after another, like a row or run.

clue.text: Legal profession upsetting Bertha

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, so the name is overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: Lawyers causing distress to a woman called Bertha.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertha is not a person here, only six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers collectively are called the Bar, after the rail dividing the courtroom where they plead.

clue.text: Old landholders in Athens displaced

indicators.note: displaced things are moved from their places, so the city's letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: Ancient Greek property owners driven out of their city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek setting points to the wrong country: thanes were Anglo-Saxon and Scottish nobles, as in Macbeth, Thane of Cawdor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanes held land granted by a king in return for service in early medieval Britain.

clue.text: Make merry outside a show

indicators.note: the merrymaking word goes outside, wrapping round the single letter 'a'

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate noisily

explanation.surface: Revellers partying on the street outside a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' seems to be a noun, a performance; it is the verb, to disclose.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to display or uncover it so others can see it.

clue.text: The French hut held together with rope?

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut

explanation.surface: A rickety French cabin kept standing only by rope.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that rope is only one way of tying things; the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashed means bound or fastened tightly with cord, as sailors secure cargo on deck.

clue.text: Member of religious community has been wicked, incited evil

indicators.note: wicked behaviour is bad, and badly treated letters come out in a corrupted order
a second word for badness, doubling the signal that the neighbouring words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A scandal: a monk accused of wickedness and of stirring up evil.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is split around the first indicator: 'been' and 'incited' together, with 'wicked' and 'evil' both saying shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Benedictines are monks and nuns following the Rule of Saint Benedict, a Catholic order.

clue.text: Husband facing wrath, one to go in wardrobe?

indicators.note: the husband faces, so stands in front of, the wrath

explanation.surface: A husband hiding in the wardrobe from an angry spouse, farce-style.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the husband himself hides in the wardrobe; the question mark marks a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat hanger is the frame on which clothes hang inside a wardrobe.

clue.text: Lord that is holy person, coming before all others

parts.note: an earl is a peer, a lord
i.e. = id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A lord who is a holy man and takes precedence over everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma separates the wordplay from the definition, which is a superlative phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest is first in time, preceding every other item or event.

clue.text: Appear to give notice before end of term

indicators.note: the noticing comes first, placed ahead of the last letter
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter of 'term' is kept

explanation.surface: A student asked to present themselves before the term ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give notice' tempts as a resignation phrase; 'to give' merely joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give an impression or look a certain way to observers.

clue.text: Quiet fool in sandy area turned and entered forbidden territory

indicators.note: the quiet fool sits in the sandy area, so goes inside it
something turned round faces the other way, so the sandy area is read backwards

parts.note: a desert is a sandy wasteland
p = piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A silly person wandering into an off-limits stretch of sand, then turning back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' applies only to the sandy area, which is reversed before the quiet fool is placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to go onto land or property without the owner's permission.

clue.text: Resist pests, horrible semi-siblings

indicators.note: a horrible mess is disordered, so these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cinderella told to stand up to her pesky, horrible relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrible' seems to describe the siblings, as Cinderella's are; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepsisters are related only by a parent's marriage, not by blood, so half-sisters in a loose sense.

clue.text: Joke I'd spun with attempt to show expertise

parts.note: a pun is a play on words, a joke

indicators.note: spun round, the two letters of 'I'd' turn to face the other way

parts.note: the letters of I'd, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A comedian spinning a gag in an effort to look clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' strings the pieces in order; only the middle one is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Punditry is the learned opinion offered by experts or commentators on a subject.

clue.text: Friend nabbed by gang is getting better

indicators.note: whatever is nabbed is held, so the friend goes inside the gang

parts.note: a ring is a criminal gang, as in a smuggling ring

explanation.surface: A kidnapped friend recovering after being grabbed by a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gang' has to be RING, the sense in 'drug ring', not MOB or CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient or market rallying is recovering strength after a setback.

clue.text: Note Queen leading state

indicators.note: in a down clue what leads comes first, so the queen goes on top

parts.note: Qu is a standard abbreviation for queen
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A monarch at the head of her country writing a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' reads as a written message and 'state' as a country; one is musical, the other a verb. A quaver is the British name for an eighth note.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaver is a musical note lasting half a crotchet, an eighth note in American terms.

clue.text: Old Roman vehicle bypassing deep track

indicators.note: a bypass goes round something, so the vehicle wraps round the track

parts.note: a rut is a deep groove worn by wheels

explanation.surface: A Roman chariot avoiding a sunken road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman setting suggests a chariot for 'vehicle'; it is a modern bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Brutus was the Roman senator among Julius Caesar's assassins.

clue.text: London arcade in which Heather is embraced by actor Richard?

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms round someone, so the actor's surname goes round the plant

parts.note: Richard Burton, the Welsh film actor

explanation.surface: In a London shopping arcade, a woman named Heather hugged by a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant. BURLINGTON Arcade is a covered shopping passage off Piccadilly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burlington Arcade is a famous Regency-era covered shopping street in Mayfair.

clue.text: Insect given clouts when flying around

indicators.note: things flying around are scattered in the air, so these letters come down in a new order

explanation.surface: A buzzing bug getting swatted as it flies about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying around' fits an insect so well that it seems descriptive; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A locust is a grasshopper species that swarms and devours crops.

clue.text: Sleep with relations under a cloth

indicators.note: in a down clue the relations sit under the sleep, so they come second

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A family napping together beneath one blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep with relations' sounds improper; 'with' just joins two pieces, stacked as a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin is a small square of fabric for wiping the mouth at table.

clue.text: Bird left Noah's vessel

parts.note: the Ark, Noah's boat in Genesis

explanation.surface: A bird flying away from Noah's Ark, as in the flood story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as the verb 'departed'; it is just the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a songbird, the skylark famous for singing while it rises high.

clue.text: Nasty notice involving six being kicked out of home?

indicators.note: something nasty has been messed up, so the letters of the notice are disordered
to involve is to take in, so the shuffled notice takes the number inside it

explanation.surface: A cruel notice ordering six people out of their home.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is an eviction notice, so the answer is in plain sight; the question mark marks the definition as descriptive.
explanation.definitionFit: Eviction is the legal removal of a tenant from a property they occupy.

clue.text: Hallucinogenic drug making one play around in waste water

indicators.note: the plaything goes in the waste water, which holds it
turned around, the plaything is read backwards

parts.note: a toy is a thing one plays with

explanation.surface: A drug that makes a user fool about in sewage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste water' suggests sewage; here it is a polite name for urine.
explanation.definitionFit: Peyote is a small Mexican cactus containing mescaline, used for visions.

clue.text: Short break with nothing right in seaside town?

indicators.note: nothing and right are put in the short break, which holds them

parts.note: a rest is a short break

explanation.surface: A quick holiday with no proper plans at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short break' reads as a holiday, fitting the seaside; it is REST. The question mark says a resort need not be by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a holiday destination town, often on the coast, visited for leisure.

clue.text: American soldier leading workers, huge folk

indicators.note: the soldier leads, so comes at the front of the workers

parts.note: a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US army sergeant in charge of a squad of big labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' is ANTS, the insect caste, not men or hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Giants are beings of enormous stature from myth and folklore.
